Prepare Review Subsets from Person and Class Incident Reports

prepareSubsetInfo.Rd

Translate incident reports into exact person–item pairs for visualSubsetRecode. Class reports are expanded using class membership and, for block selections, each person's booklet. Incident provenance is retained when reports overlap.

Usage

prepareSubsetInfo(dat, issues, persons = NULL, booklets = NULL,
                  blocks = NULL, rotation = NULL, subunits = NULL,
                  ID = "ID", classID = "classId")

# S3 method for class 'preparedSubsetInfo'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

dat

Data frame of responses in wide format, with unique, nonmissing person IDs.

issues

A data frame with one row per incident and these columns:

issueId

Unique, nonmissing incident identifier.

level

Either "person" or "class".

targetId

Person ID or class ID, according to level.

scope

Either "item", "block", or "blockPosition".

target

A single item name, block name, or positive integer block position, according to scope. A character column accommodates mixed scopes.

comment

Optional description; missing comments are allowed.

persons

Required for class reports: a data frame with columns named by ID and classID, with one row per person. Class IDs must be unique across schools; combine school and class identifiers beforehand if needed.

booklets

Booklet design with booklet and columns block1, block2, etc. Column suffixes determine positions, regardless of column order. Empty or missing block entries represent unoccupied positions.

blocks

Block design with block, subunit, and subunitBlockPosition. Items and positions must be unique within blocks.

rotation

Person-to-booklet mapping with columns named by ID and booklet, with one row per person.

subunits

Optional mapping with unique subunit and corresponding subunitRecoded names. Each selected item must match exactly one raw or recoded column in dat. Aggregated item names are not inferred.

ID

Person identifier column name. Must differ from classID and reserved incident/output column names. Default: "ID".

classID

Class identifier column in persons. Default: "classId".

object

A result from prepareSubsetInfo.

...

Reserved for additional summary arguments.

Details

For block or block-position reports, supply all three design tables booklets, blocks, and rotation. A named block can appear at different positions for different people; a block position can refer to different blocks. Item-only reports do not require design tables. When design tables are supplied, item selections are also checked against each person's booklet.

The function stops on unknown classes, persons absent from dat, unresolved items, ambiguous mappings, and targets not administered to a selected person. It never silently drops class members or guesses assignments. Inspect and resolve these reports before starting a review. Empty report tables are rejected.

Numeric identifiers retain enough precision to distinguish the stored values throughout preparation and review. Character identifiers are matched exactly. Import identifiers as character when leading zeros or digits beyond numeric precision must be preserved; precision already lost during import cannot be recovered.

The returned table contains one row per incident/person/item. An overlapping cell appears once for each incident that selected it. There is no automatic priority between individual and class reports. In this first version each report selects one target; explicit person exceptions and decisions with different replacement values per incident are not implemented. Pausing, automatic checkpoints and resuming a review are provided by visualSubsetRecode.

Value

prepareSubsetInfo returns a data frame of class preparedSubsetInfo with columns issueId, the person ID, datCols, level, targetId, scope, target, block, blockPosition, subunitBlockPosition, and comment. The ID column name is retained as an attribute. Without design tables, block metadata is missing.

Pass this object directly to visualSubsetRecode; incident grouping, ID column, comments, and available positions are selected automatically. summary returns a data frame with one row per incident, its level and target ID, counts of persons, items and cells, and overlappingCells: the number of its cells also selected by another incident. Counts include cells containing NA.

See also

visualSubsetRecode, inputList, vignette("subset_review", package = "eatPrep")

Examples

dat <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), I1 = c(1, 0), I2 = c(0, 1))
persons <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), classId = "K1")
booklets <- data.frame(booklet = c("X", "Y"),
                       block1 = c("A", "B"), block2 = c("B", "A"))
blocks <- data.frame(subunit = c("I1", "I2"), block = c("A", "B"),
                     subunitBlockPosition = 1)
rotation <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), booklet = c("X", "Y"))
issues <- data.frame(
  issueId = c("V1", "V2"), level = c("class", "person"),
  targetId = c("K1", "P1"), scope = c("blockPosition", "item"),
  target = c("1", "I1"), comment = c("Audio failure", NA)
)
info <- prepareSubsetInfo(dat, issues, persons, booklets, blocks, rotation)
info
#>   issueId ID datCols  level targetId         scope target block blockPosition
#> 1      V1 P1      I1  class       K1 blockPosition      1     A             1
#> 2      V1 P2      I2  class       K1 blockPosition      1     B             1
#> 3      V2 P1      I1 person       P1          item     I1     A             1
#>   subunitBlockPosition       comment
#> 1                    1 Audio failure
#> 2                    1 Audio failure
#> 3                    1          <NA>
summary(info)
#>   issueId  level targetId persons items cells overlappingCells
#> 1      V1  class       K1       2     2     2                1
#> 2      V2 person       P1       1     1     1                1
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- visualSubsetRecode(dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci")
result$dat
result$subsetInfo
} # }
